## Adversarial angles the critics were pointed at

The plan's central argument is that the refresh's own `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` flock already bounds refresh concurrency to one fleet-wide, so counting it toward the cap protects nothing. The Methodology critic is tasked with verifying that claim end to end against `acquire_refresh_lock` / `cmd_refresh` — including whether the lock is held for the heavy pytest's whole duration and whether two worktree roots could take two different locks — because the whole fix rests on it. Both critics are additionally pointed at the plan's weakest-looking step: its claim that the post-fix worst case (cap-many gates + a refresh) is "a state the fail-open arm can already produce today", when today that state is reachable only AFTER a session burns the bounded 2700 s wait and post-fix it is reachable immediately. If "already reachable" is not the same as "reachable at the same rate", the cap-purpose-survives argument is weaker than §3 states.
